# Phase banner

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a phase banner to show that a service is in alpha or beta and give users a way to provide feedback.

## When to use

- Use when a public service is genuinely in alpha or beta and users should understand its development status.
- Provide a working feedback route that the team monitors and can act on.

## When not to use

- Do not use a phase banner as a substitute for explaining known limitations or service availability.
- Do not retain an alpha or beta label after the service no longer meets that lifecycle stage.

## Anatomy

- **Banner container (required):** A govuk-phase-banner sits inside the standard width context near the top of the page.
- **Phase tag (required):** A GOV.UK Tag contains the current phase label.
- **Feedback message (required):** Short text explains that the service is developing and contains a feedback link.

## Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Alpha | `div` | `govuk-phase-banner` | An alpha service being tested and iterated. |
| Beta | `div` | `govuk-phase-banner` | A beta service available to users while continuing to improve. |

## Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- No GOV.UK JavaScript module is required.
- Place the banner consistently below the header or service navigation and before main content.
- The feedback link must work without JavaScript.

## Accessibility contract

- The phase is visible text inside the tag rather than a colour-only badge.
- Use descriptive feedback-link text when the surrounding sentence would not be announced with it.
- Preserve link focus and visited-state behaviour.

## Content rules

- Use the actual service phase label, usually “Alpha” or “Beta”.
- Keep the message short and explain that feedback helps improve the service.
- Link directly to the feedback mechanism rather than a generic homepage.

## Token references

- `govuk.color.border`
- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.spacing.static.2`

## HTML examples

### Alpha phase banner

```html
<div class="govuk-phase-banner">
  <p class="govuk-phase-banner__content">
    <strong class="govuk-tag govuk-phase-banner__content__tag">Alpha</strong>
    <span class="govuk-phase-banner__text">This is a new service – your <a href="/feedback" class="govuk-link">feedback</a> will help us to improve it.</span>
  </p>
</div>
```
